name: develop-like-sudipta
description: Battle-tested development discipline plugin. Enforces 11 engineering pillars via skills, agents, hooks, and commands. v4.3.3 fixes the portability bug in the bundled scheduled-task SKILLs — they previously hardcoded the maintainer's dev workspace path (`/Users/sudipta/Workspace/...`) and would silently fail on any other machine when cron fired. Two-part fix: (1) `install.sh` now copies `aggregate_learnings.sh` + `distill_learnings.sh` from `<plugin>/skills/autoresearch/scripts/` into `~/.cache/ccbridge/` alongside the rest of the bridge — same install-managed canonical location as watchdog/audit/learning. (2) Bundled SKILL.md files in `assets/scheduled-tasks/` now reference `~/.cache/ccbridge/aggregate_learnings.sh` and `~/.cache/ccbridge/distill_learnings.sh` — stable per-machine paths independent of where the plugin lives on disk, with a presence-check that nudges users to `/ccbridge-init` if the scripts are missing. Also: swept remaining `/Users/sudipta/Workspace/...` occurrences in `ccbridge-init.md` and `substrate_and_access.md` to use `~/Workspace/...` so prose works on any Mac. Cleanup: stale smoke-test entries (`v43-smoke`, `v432-fake-ws-3`) purged from the canonical `~/.cache/ccbridge/projects.json` on the dev Mac. Live Cowork scheduled tasks on this machine refreshed to the new prompt via `mcp__scheduled-tasks__update_scheduled_task`. v4.3.2 closes the silent learning-loss foot-gun: `start_watchdog.sh` now has three-layer WORKSPACE resolution — (1) honor explicit env var when set (back-compat), (2) auto-detect by scanning `ps -axo pid=,command=` for processes whose argv[0] ends in `/claude` AND path does NOT contain `Claude.app/` (correctly distinguishes a real terminal-mode CC from any Cowork-embedded CC instances), then reading the cwd of that PID via `lsof -a -p <pid> -d cwd`, (3) fail-fast with a loud error pointing at three fixes if neither produces a workspace. Bonus: when WORKSPACE is known, `register_project.sh` runs IMMEDIATELY on watchdog start (no lazy registration on first event) and a `watchdog_recovery outcome=started` learning event fires — so a new workspace appears in `~/.cache/ccbridge/projects.json` AND the central tail before any prompt is approved. Net effect: any future run of `start_watchdog.sh` (with or without explicit WORKSPACE) either captures correctly or refuses to start. The previous silent-but-keystroke-pressing failure mode (watchdog working as a keyboard but never logging a single state/learning event because the env-guard inside watchdog.sh quietly dropped them) is no longer reachable. v4.3.1 ships `/ccbridge-init` — one idempotent slash command per machine that completes the v4.3 closed-loop setup with zero manual steps: runs the bundled `setup_ccbridge.sh` (delegates to `install.sh` to copy the latest bridge scripts including the v4.3 `register_project.sh` + `learning.sh` into `~/.cache/ccbridge/`, creates the `learnings/aggregated/distillation/` subdirs, bootstraps an empty `projects.json`, AND copies the two bundled scheduled-task SKILL folders from `assets/scheduled-tasks/` into `~/Documents/Claude/Scheduled/`), then calls `mcp__scheduled-tasks__list_scheduled_tasks` to inventory current Cowork tasks, and either creates (`mcp__scheduled-tasks__create_scheduled_task` with recommended crons — aggregate at 02:15 daily, distill at 03:30 every Sunday) or refreshes (`mcp__scheduled-tasks__update_scheduled_task` preserving any user-customized cron) each task's prompt to match the bundled SKILL.md. Re-runs after every plugin update are safe — `cp -f` for scripts/SKILLs and check-before-create for Cowork tasks. `install.sh` SCRIPTS array updated with `register_project.sh` + `learning.sh`. Workflow on a new machine: `git pull` or reinstall the .plugin → run `/ccbridge-init` in Cowork → done; nightly + weekly tasks now run themselves. v4.3.0 closes the runtime-learning loop: every workspace that uses the plugin auto-registers in `~/.cache/ccbridge/projects.json` on first command invocation (`register_project.sh` hashes the absolute workspace path → 16-hex id), and a new `learning.sh` script dual-writes structured events to both `<workspace>/.cc/learnings.jsonl` (local debuggable) and `~/.cache/ccbridge/learnings/<id>.jsonl` (central tail swept by the scheduled aggregator). Seven runtime capture points wired in: watchdog (refusal patterns + auto-approved snippets), audit.sh (clean/drift/hard_error outcomes), bug-triage agent (classification + signature), verify_gate (red tier + assertion AND green durations), /cc-drive (substrate choice + reason), /browser-test (per-phase outcome + browser + duration), /reproduce-bug (seeded/resolved stage pairs). Two new scheduled tasks: `ccbridge-aggregate-learnings` (nightly — merges all tails into dated jsonl files via cursor-based incremental sweep) and `ccbridge-distill-and-propose` (weekly — turns 7-day aggregates into a top-N-signatures-per-category markdown report, flags cross-project signals where signature appears in ≥2 workspaces, optionally triggers an autoresearch run with the distilled priors). No api.anthropic.com calls — all reasoning runs through the user's Claude subscription via Cowork scheduled tasks. v4.2.1 closes the autoresearch loop's last gap: the main run_autoresearch.sh now actually calls propose_hypothesis.sh per iteration (was previously a v4.1 stub that required external mutation). v4.2 closes the autoresearch backlog: real proposer (file-based + API-based via curl to api.anthropic.com), opt-in LLM-based scoring with Claude Haiku-4.5 + caching + cost guard, all per-skill scorers normalized to F1 in [0,1] for cross-skill comparability, distributed swarm scaffolding (shared scoreboard + manual merge — full SETI@home is v5.0+), bash 3.2 compatibility audit (clean), and two pre-existing audit.sh bugs fixed (awk Commit-pattern range collapse + shallow-repo silent failure). v4.1 introduces Karpathy-style autoresearch: every skill ships with an autoresearch/ subdirectory (program.md goal + score.sh metric + target.txt editable file), the new `autoresearch` meta-skill drives the loop (read program → propose mutation → score → commit if better, reset if worse), and 4 new slash commands (/autoresearch, /autoresearch-status, /autoresearch-resume, /autoresearch-baseline) operate on any wired skill. Baselines: sd-claude-code-access F1=0.78, develop-like-sudipta acc=47.91, code-hacker F1=0.31 — substantial headroom for overnight self-improvement. v4.0 completes the hardening cycle: 3 specialized agents (audit / bug-triage / playwright-spec-reviewer), 2 git hooks enforcing bug-TDD discipline at commit time, cross-browser/mobile Playwright projects, opt-in axe-playwright a11y assertions, WebSocket/SSE/HTTP-streaming testing patterns, worktree-aware orchestration, human-checkpoint cadence with pause_at config, automated stale-spec detection via source-hash compare, screenshot+spec archival, and eval coverage for substrate / verify-gate / bug-TDD trigger phrases. v3.4 expands the CC-driver toolkit: GitHub Actions e2e workflow auto-emission, structured test-output parsing across pytest/jest/vitest/cargo/go/maven, flake retry + whitelist, auth-state freshness checks, dev-server orchestration with auto-start, data-testid directive enforcement, API-level testing for backend-only phases, and SSH/remote-Mac substrate (Path D). v3.3 hardens the CC-driver: per-project danger-pattern extensions + watchdog dryrun mode, commit-lag-aware audit retry, watchdog refusal escalation to .cc/escalations.log (with optional ESCALATE_CMD hook), and a state.json salvage script for corrupted JSONL recovery. v3.2 adds substrate detection — every CC-driving session starts by probing which MCPs are available (Desktop_Commander preferred, computer-use fallback with request_access for Terminal at tier 'click', manual as last resort) and surfaces the chosen path to the user before driving anything; the previous versions silently assumed bash + osascript would reach the Mac. v3.1 mandates a verify gate (static checks + unit/integration tests via pytest/jest/vitest/cargo/go-test/etc., auto-detected per project) before browser-test; opens Claude in Chrome only when unit tests are green. When ANY test goes red — unit or browser — bug-driven TDD kicks in: write a NEW failing pytest case AND a NEW failing Playwright step that both reproduce the bug, confirm both red, send the fix directive to CC, then confirm green on the new unit test, the new browser test, the full verify-gate (regression guard), and the original phase test. No fix lands without a failing test first. Bundles the sd-claude-code-access skill — drive Claude Code from Cowork end-to-end with file-based directives, permission-prompt watchdog, hang recovery, resume-after-crash, per-phase real-browser verification, Playwright spec emission into the project's docs/e2e-testing/, and audit tooling to verify the discipline was followed. Works WITH superpowers plugin. Sources: Google SRE, DORA, OWASP, Fowler, Thoughtworks.
